newsitem.title: USA: CME live cattle end down weaker cash, beef values.
newsitem.headline: CME live cattle end down weaker cash, beef values.

text.p: A dip in choice-grade wholesale boxed beef prices at noon after days of gains, coupled with an easier tone to cash cattle prices, pressured CME live cattle futures to the day's lows by the close, traders said.
Feeder cattle also finished weaker in light dealings.
Live cattle punched through technical support early and trended lower most of the day to finish weak, as an easier tone to cash cattle values weighed on sentiment.
Lower choice beef quotes at noon after a recent runup to 3-1/2 year highs and a weaker tone to cash cattle were cited, traders said.
Commercial pressure was evident and added to long liquidation to take futures lower, they said.
Live cattle closed off 0.475 cent a lb to up 0.125 cent with only distant December up and nearby December off most at 67.275 cents.

The market expected beef prices to soften, especially coming into the Thanksgiving Day holiday next week. Recent gains in choice beef prices were already starting to temper retailer demand and interest for beef will be even less as they turn their interest to more traditional holiday meats such as turkeys and hams, sources said.
The lighter-weight choice boxed beef value rose to $120.74 per cwt Tuesday, the highest level since June 17, 1993, before slipping at Wednesday's noon report.
